verdicts.reason: A keeps the brand panel with a legible sun logo and wordmark, and the headline, rule, body and CTA all sit cleanly on one centered axis. Its weakness is vertical crowding: the eyebrow, headline, rule, body copy, CTA and legal text are packed together with little breathing room, and the legal line runs close to the bottom edge. In B, the orange divider rule cuts straight through "Yet" in the headline, which is a clear collision. B's logo and wordmark have also shrunk until they can't be read, its oversized dark panel is mostly empty, and the headline runs almost into the panel edge.
